response_text:
4. (Currently Amended) A method of impeding Leishmania transmission in __canine subjects__ by administering to a canine subject a composition comprising a Fucose Mannose Ligand (FML) fraction from Leishmania donovani and saponin.

5. (Currently Amended) Use of the composition of claim 4 for preparation of a blocking vaccine to impede Leishmania transmission in canine subjects.

6. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 4 wherein said composition further comprises suitable pharmacological vehicles, for blocking Leishmania transmission in canine subjects.

7. (Currently Amended) The composition of claim 4, wherein the Leishmania donovani promastigotes or amastigotes fractions called "Fucose Mannose Ligand" (FML) comprise a glycoprotein complex containing 29% of neutral sugar, 44% of protein, 11% of phosphate and hexoamines traces composed by protein bands with molecular weight ranging from 9 to 95 kDa, some protein bands having carbohydrates at 36 and 54 to 68 kDa, the FML glycidic portion presenting 10% of fucose and 47% of mannose, 30% of glucose, 12% of galactose and xylose traces, aminoacids containing 10 to 20% of glutamic acid, alanine, aspartic acid and glycine, 5 to 10% of serine, histidine, lysine, leucine, threonine, proline and valine, and 2 to 5% of arginine, methionine, isoleucine, tyrosine and phenylalanine.
